A PDF studio that never sees your files

Most online PDF tools upload your documents to their servers to process them — contracts, bank statements, IDs and all. PDF Studio does the work right here in your browser using the same open-source engines your browser uses to show PDFs. Nothing is uploaded, nothing is stored, and once the page has loaded it even works offline.

  1. Add PDFs and images — drop them in, choose them, or paste.
  2. Arrange — drag pages into order, rotate the sideways ones, remove the ones you don’t need.
  3. Download one PDF, split it into several, or save the pages as images.
Are my files really not uploaded?

Really. The PDF engines run inside this page, and the page makes no network requests while you work — you can switch off Wi-Fi after it loads and everything still works. Open your browser’s developer tools and watch the Network tab if you’d like to check.

Is there a size or page limit?

There’s no artificial limit — no daily caps and no “Pro” tier. The only limit is your device’s memory: hundreds of pages are fine on a laptop or a recent phone.

Can it open password-protected PDFs?

Yes. If a PDF needs a password to open, you’ll be asked for it, and it’s only used on your device. PDFs that open freely but block editing (common for bank statements) are handled automatically. The pages you download are saved without the protection.

Will links, text and quality be preserved?

Yes. Pages are copied exactly — text stays selectable and searchable, and nothing is re-compressed. Only images you add are converted, and only if you choose “Smaller file”. Bookmarks from the original files aren’t carried over when merging.

Does it work on iPhone and Android?

Yes. Tap to select pages, press and hold a page to drag it, and photos straight from your camera roll — including iPhone HEIC photos in Safari — become PDF pages.
